about.en:
42 Berlin is the Berlin campus of 42, the network of tuition-free computer-science schools founded in Paris in 2013 with more than 50 campuses in over 30 countries. There are no teachers, lectures or fees: students learn by building projects and reviewing each other's code, and the campus is usually open 24/7.

Anyone aged 18 or over can apply, with no diploma or previous coding experience required. You register online, take a short logic/aptitude test, attend an introduction session and then a full-time, on-site four-week 'Piscine' (selection bootcamp in C and shell). The next selection Piscine listed on the campus site runs 8 February - 5 March 2027. Those who succeed join the core curriculum (about 12-18 months) and can then specialise (AI, cybersecurity, graphics, etc.), with internships along the way.

Teaching is in English. Tuition is free; students cover their own housing and living costs and, for non-residents, visa requirements.

42 Roma Luiss is the Rome campus of 42, the network of tuition-free computer-science schools founded in Paris in 2013 with more than 50 campuses in over 30 countries. There are no teachers, lectures or fees: students learn by building projects and reviewing each other's code, and the campus is usually open 24/7.

Anyone aged 18 or over can apply, with no diploma or previous coding experience required. You register online, take a short logic/aptitude test, attend an introduction session and then a full-time, on-site four-week 'Piscine' (selection bootcamp in C and shell). The next selection Piscine listed on the campus site runs 8 February - 5 March 2027. Those who succeed join the core curriculum (about 12-18 months) and can then specialise (AI, cybersecurity, graphics, etc.), with internships along the way.

Teaching is in English. Tuition is free; students cover their own housing and living costs and, for non-residents, visa requirements.

about.en:
42 Barcelona is the Barcelona campus of 42, the network of tuition-free computer-science schools founded in Paris in 2013 with more than 50 campuses in over 30 countries. There are no teachers, lectures or fees: students learn by building projects and reviewing each other's code, and the campus is usually open 24/7.

Anyone aged 18 or over can apply, with no diploma or previous coding experience required. You register online, take a short logic/aptitude test, attend an introduction session and then a full-time, on-site four-week 'Piscine' (selection bootcamp in C and shell). Piscine sessions are scheduled several times a year; the campus site lists upcoming dates after you register. Those who succeed join the core curriculum (about 12-18 months) and can then specialise (AI, cybersecurity, graphics, etc.), with internships along the way.

Teaching is in Spanish and English. Tuition is free; students cover their own housing and living costs and, for non-residents, visa requirements.

about.en:
Gen-E is JA Europe's annual entrepreneurship festival, bringing together the best student companies and start-ups from across Europe. It is the final stage of the JA Company Programme (secondary school) and Start Up Programme (higher education), in which teams create and run a real mini-company during the school year.

The road has four stages: running your company in school (September–May), the year-round Virtual Gen-E online expo with online awards, national competitions in front of expert juries (January–May), and the in-person festival in Luxembourg on 6-9 July 2027, where national champions exhibit, pitch on stage and compete for European awards such as the JA Europe Company of the Year.

Participation is through the national JA organisation in your country (JA operates in 40+ European countries, including Georgia through JA Georgia). Teams usually pay no fee; national winners are supported to attend the festival.

Classes meet in Birmingham, Glasgow, London, Manchester, Sheffield and Cape Town. Eligibility: over 18, low income (below 60% of regional median after housing and taxes), living within 90 minutes by public transport of a hub, and passing a free English test.

about.en:
FASPE (Fellowships at Auschwitz for the Study of Professional Ethics) brings small cohorts of graduate students and early-career professionals to Berlin, Kraków and the Auschwitz memorial site. By studying how doctors, lawyers, business leaders, journalists, engineers and clergy contributed to the crimes of Nazi Germany, fellows examine the ethical choices they will face in their own professions today.

There are six programmes: Law, Business and Design & Technology run 28 May – 11 June 2027; Medical, Clergy & Religious Leaders and Journalism run 18 June – 2 July 2027. Seminars are led by expert faculty, and fellows join a lifelong alumni network and later workshops.

The fellowship is fully funded: FASPE covers round-trip airfare (also for fellows travelling from outside the United States), hotels, group meals, admission fees, local transport and pocket money. Applications close on 3 January 2027 via Submittable.

It only accepts submissions from companies registered in UNICEF programme countries (the list is on the site; it includes many countries in Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Eastern Europe). Startups must be willing to release their technology as open source.

Companies can send an expression of interest at any time, and UNICEF also runs thematic calls with deadlines; after an EOI there is a request for proposal stage over the following months.

about.en:
42 Firenze is the Florence campus of 42, the network of tuition-free computer-science schools founded in Paris in 2013 with more than 50 campuses in over 30 countries. There are no teachers, lectures or fees: students learn by building projects and reviewing each other's code, and the campus is usually open 24/7.

Anyone aged 18 or over can apply, with no diploma or previous coding experience required. You register online, take a short logic/aptitude test, attend an introduction session and then a full-time, on-site four-week 'Piscine' (selection bootcamp in C and shell). Piscine sessions are scheduled several times a year; the campus site lists upcoming dates after you register. Those who succeed join the core curriculum (about 12-18 months) and can then specialise (AI, cybersecurity, graphics, etc.), with internships along the way.

Teaching is in Italian and English. Tuition is free; students cover their own housing and living costs and, for non-residents, visa requirements.

42 Le Havre is the Le Havre campus of 42, the network of tuition-free computer-science schools founded in Paris in 2013 with more than 50 campuses in over 30 countries. There are no teachers, lectures or fees: students learn by building projects and reviewing each other's code, and the campus is usually open 24/7.

Anyone aged 18 or over can apply, with no diploma or previous coding experience required. You register online, take a short logic/aptitude test, attend an introduction session and then a full-time, on-site four-week 'Piscine' (selection bootcamp in C and shell). Piscine sessions are scheduled several times a year; the campus site lists upcoming dates after you register. Those who succeed join the core curriculum (about 12-18 months) and can then specialise (AI, cybersecurity, graphics, etc.), with internships along the way.

Teaching is in French and English. Tuition is free; students cover their own housing and living costs and, for non-residents, visa requirements.

about.en:

Alongside its core programme it runs specialised cohorts with partners (for example a deep-tech cohort with a quantum focus launched with the University of Chicago). Founders from outside the US have participated, with much of the programme available remotely.

Applications are rolling via the 'Tell us what you are building' form on the website; Alchemist typically invests a small amount in exchange for equity.

about.en:
The United Nations Young Leaders Online Training Programme is run by UNITAR's Multilateral Diplomacy division. The January 2027 edition is web-based and runs from 4 to 29 January 2027 (28 days), combining recorded and live sessions with UN and diplomacy practitioners.

It covers how the UN system works, multilateral diplomacy and negotiation, the Sustainable Development Goals, leadership, gender equality and youth engagement. It suits students and young professionals interested in international organisations; participants who complete the course receive a UNITAR certificate, and UNITAR offers an optional follow-up field visit to Geneva.

The course fee is US$750. Registration closes on 24 December 2026; further editions are planned for April, June and August 2027.
